name: Proton–proton chain, step 1
note: The first, slowest step of the chain that powers the Sun — converts two protons into deuterium.

name: Deuterium + deuterium → helium-3
note: One of two equally likely D–D fusion branches.

name: Deuterium + deuterium → tritium
note: The other D–D fusion branch, producing tritium instead.

name: Deuterium + tritium → helium-4
note: The easiest fusion reaction to ignite — the leading candidate for practical fusion power (ITER, NIF).

name: Helium-3 + helium-3 → helium-4
note: The pp-chain's final step, producing ordinary helium-4 and two protons.

name: Lithium-6 + neutron → tritium
note: How tritium fuel is bred inside a fusion reactor blanket.

name: Lithium-7 + proton → 2 helium-4
note: The first artificially induced nuclear reaction (Cockcroft & Walton, 1932) — 'splitting the atom' with a particle accelerator.

name: Carbon-12 + proton → nitrogen-13 (CNO cycle)
note: First step of the CNO cycle — the dominant fusion pathway in stars heavier than the Sun. The released energy leaves as a gamma-ray photon.

name: Uranium-235 fission (one channel)
note: One of many possible product pairs when U-235 splits after absorbing a slow neutron — the reaction that powers most nuclear reactors and the first atomic bomb.

name: Uranium-235 fission (another channel)
note: A different real fragment pair from the same U-235 + n reaction — fission products vary statistically, not just one path.

name: Plutonium-239 fission (one channel)
note: Pu-239, bred from U-238 in reactors, is the other major fission fuel/weapons material.
